chains.name: Electrification & grid equipment
chains.thesis: Grid build-out, datacenters, EVs and reshored manufacturing collide with transformer and switchgear lead times measured in years. The equipment makers price the scarcity through backlog and margin — copper is an input COST to them, not a revenue driver, which is exactly why they belong in a different book from the miners.

commodity.spot_source: no commodity — the regime read is the backlog/book-to-bill cycle and transformer lead times. Copper (HGUSD) is an INPUT COST here: rising copper is a margin headwind, never a revenue tailwind. proxy_etf GRID feed-verified 2026-07-27

chains.notes: The EQUIPMENT half of v1.3's copper_electrification, assembled with power_for_ai's grid-equipment layer. All four industry strings PROVEN live 2026-07-27: Electrical Equipment & Parts (ETN/HUBB/NVT/POWL), Industrial - Specialties (AZZ), Engineering & Construction (PWR), Industrial - Machinery (v1.3). SPLIT RULE: a producer or royalty_streamer mapping here is a mapping error — printed and dropped. PWR screens here but its primary chain is power_for_ai (EPC/interconnection is power delivery); 2-chain within this book is legal.

chains.name: Nuclear — SMRs & reactor services
chains.thesis: Datacenter load growth made firm, carbon-free baseload a procurement problem, and SMRs are the only new supply that fits behind a meter this decade. Value accrues on DATED regulatory and construction milestones — NRC design approval, COL, first concrete, first criticality — years before revenue, so the component and fuel-service incumbents monetize the ramp long before the developers do.

commodity.spot_source: no spot — the regime read is the NRC/COL dateline track plus datacenter-PPA flow. Uranium is MINING's business, not this chain's: an SMR developer is not a uranium play. proxy_etf NLR feed-verified 2026-07-27

chains.notes: Industry strings PROVEN live 2026-07-27 and DELIBERATELY BROAD because FMP files this cohort inconsistently: BWXT=Aerospace & Defense, SMR=Renewable Utilities, OKLO=Independent Power Producers, NNE=Electrical Equipment & Parts. (The spec's proposed 'Regulated Electric' is WRONG — OKLO does not carry it and it would drag in DUK/SO-class regulated utilities as pure noise.) The breadth is deliberate: the chain map's physical-anchor rule does the precision work, and this chain overlaps power_for_ai and electrification_grid by construction — 2-chain within the book is legal, the map assigns the primary. LANE-B-HEAVY BY DESIGN: SMR developers are pre-FCF and enter on dated NRC/COL/first-concrete milestones under the unchanged lane-B runway gate. A thin Lane A (BWXT-class only) is the EXPECTED outcome, not a failure — the v1.3 quantum precedent verbatim.

chains.name: Power for AI
chains.thesis: Datacenter load growth outruns grid interconnection; whoever can deliver firm electrons or the equipment to make them — turbines, transformers, switchgear, nuclear-levered IPPs, grid EPC — sells into a queue measured in years.

commodity.spot_source: FMP commodities (Henry Hub front month) — the fuel-cost driver for IPP spark spreads, not a revenue driver

chains.notes: Carried from v1.3 with the id UNCHANGED so regime_state and ledger keys survive the split. Two layers left: grid equipment -> electrification_grid (so 'Electrical Equipment & Parts' is dropped from this screen — that is chain 1's net now), SMR developers -> nuclear_smr. Strings re-verified live 2026-07-27: GEV=Renewable Utilities; CEG/VST/TLN=Independent Power Producers; PWR=Engineering & Construction. business_model=utility (v2.0 enum addition) is the honest label for the IPP cohort that v1.3 filed awkwardly as equipment_services. Torque is margin-vs-power-prices with Henry Hub as the fuel-cost leg, never a revenue driver.

chains.name: Robotics & physical AI
chains.thesis: Labor scarcity + reshoring push factories, warehouses and surgery toward robots, and the humanoid ramp adds a new demand curve on top; the motion-control, vision, actuator and surgical-platform toll-takers monetize every deployment wave — and every robot is magnets, motors and copper windings (the demand side of this basket's metal chains).

commodity.spot_source: no commodity — the regime read is the industrial-capex cycle + humanoid program datelines; deterministic metrics use the non-commodity set (gm_trajectory/backlog), never torque

chains.notes: MIGRATED from the retired Disruptor Lens taxonomy (industry strings proven in its live runs). Industrial names here are demand-cycle cyclicals — the chain map must separate secular penetration from a capex bounce. Pre-FCF humanoid/robotics developers are lane_b via dated milestones (named production contracts, first customer deployments), never lane_a.

chains.name: Quantum computing & sensing
chains.thesis: Government programs and early enterprise contracts fund the quantum stack years before commercial breakeven; awards, named contracts and error-correction milestones are dated, idiosyncratic events that reprice names regardless of when quantum advantage actually arrives — and the cryo/photonics/control toll-takers get paid on every lab and testbed build-out either way.

commodity.spot_source: no commodity — the regime read is the government funding cycle (NQI reauthorization, DARPA/DOE programs, sovereign initiatives) + the error-correction milestone track; non-commodity metric set applies

chains.notes: The broadest industry filters in the taxonomy — this chain leans hardest on keyword hints + the chain map's physical-anchor rule; expect a high drop rate (generic hardware/semis names map low-confidence and are dropped WITH printed symbols). Pure-play platforms (IONQ/RGTI/QBTS-class) are pre-FCF -> lane_b via dated milestones (signed government awards, named enterprise/defense contracts, dated error-correction demos); an honestly tiny lane_a (FORM/COHR-class toll-takers) is the expected outcome, not a failure.

vocab_note: fmp_industries are EXACT strings from FMP /stable/available-industries — verified live 2026-07-27 against real company profiles, not guessed. Any string listed in a chain's fmp_industries_verify is NOT yet proven to return members: 0 rows there prints a WARN and the build continues; 0 rows on a PROVEN string STOPs (the anti-shrink guard). Once a live run confirms a string, delete it from fmp_industries_verify — config edit only, never code.
torque_note: torque_metrics=false chains (equipment/tech/service cohorts) get the non-commodity metric set — gm_trajectory / rev_yoy / fcf_margin / ndebt_ebitda — and NEVER fcf_torque_10pct: there is no spot price for their output to be levered to, so a torque number would be fabricated precision. Commodity chains without an FMP spot symbol still get commodity_beta_2y against their proxy_etf.
split_note: SPLIT RULE (FUTURE_RESOURCES_SPLIT_SPEC §3): business_model equipment_services|utility -> this book; producer|royalty_streamer -> mining (and is a mapping error if mapped here — printed and dropped); developer -> the book owning the physical asset being developed (an SMR developer here, a copper-mine developer in mining). royalty_streamer is NEVER legal in this book. Cross-book dual membership is FORBIDDEN — basket-dedup resolves straddlers (ties go to Mining) and the publish-time backstop STOPs on any intersection with the mining payload.
